## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Changes are needed before merge: deleting the defaults file breaks its existing loader, port validation rejects a valid boundary value, and configuration failures are hidden.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Deleting this file makes `app/startup.py::load_defaults()` raise `FileNotFoundError` whenever called; restore the file or update its loader to supply the defaults. — Existing callers can no longer load default configuration.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — `is_valid_port(65535)` returns `False` although the documented range includes 65535; change the upper comparison to `<= 65535`. — Valid configurations using TCP port 65535 are rejected.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — For malformed JSON or an unreadable configuration path, `except Exception` discards the exception and returns `{}` without any failure signal; propagate the exception or expose the failure with its cause. — Callers cannot distinguish a broken configuration from a successfully loaded empty object or diagnose the cause.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — The docstring says “returns None when h is empty,” but `normalize_host("")` executes `return ""`; align the documentation and implementation. — Callers relying on the documented `None` result will handle empty hosts incorrectly.
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — The trailing-dot branch has no test: the existing hostname test only passes `"Example.COM"`; add an assertion that `normalize_host("Example.COM.") == "example.com"`. — A regression preserving the trailing dot would pass the current suite.

## Strengths
- The added millisecond test asserts that `"1500ms"` becomes `1.5`, exercising fractional-second conversion.
- The configuration-loading test checks the parsed object from a real temporary JSON file.
